name: Hawker Hunter
summary: Elegant British swept-wing fighter, used by many air forces and now flown by US contractor adversary companies, with a few privately owned.

wings: Mid-mounted wing swept back about 35 degrees
Dogtooth leading edge on later versions
engines: Single Avon turbojet fed by wing-root intakes on each side
fuselage: Bubble canopy on a slim fuselage
Blister fairing under the front fuselage for the gun pack
tail: Swept horizontal tail mounted mid-way on the fuselage

tellTales: Wing-root intakes and a sharply pointed nose on a swept-wing jet
Bubble canopy with a long, smooth fuselage
Single large tailpipe and gun-pack blister under the nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The Sabre has a round nose intake; the Hunter has wing-root intakes.
The T-33 has straight wings and tip tanks; the Hunter has swept wings.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
